customer_context: The buyer liked the workflow but said the annual price was above budget.
actions_taken: Offered a 20% discount before quantifying value
customer_reaction: The buyer questioned the product value and used the discount as a signal that there was room to negotiate.
lessons_learned: Discounting before proving value weakened the business case and did not resolve the budget objection.

customer_context: The customer needed to reduce manual dispatch work while keeping the integration effort predictable.
customer_reaction: The buyer accepted the price after seeing payback within the first year and a credible rollout plan.
lessons_learned: For a pricing objection, proving economic value and reducing implementation uncertainty was more effective than discounting.

customer_context: The security team required evidence for auditability and data handling before approving a pilot.
customer_reaction: Security approved the pilot and operations expanded the evaluation.
lessons_learned: Security-led deals move when technical evidence is paired with a low-risk implementation path.

customer_context: The internal champion left during evaluation and the replacement owner had not yet joined the process.
actions_taken: Kept the original champion as the only active sponsor
customer_reaction: The project lost momentum after the stakeholder transition.
lessons_learned: Stakeholder changes need a mapped buying committee and a mutual action plan before momentum is lost.

customer_context: The incumbent vendor had strong relationships but weak reporting and slow support.
customer_reaction: The executive team approved a phased replacement.
lessons_learned: Competitive displacement is stronger when the conversation centers on measurable gaps instead of feature checklists.

customer_context: Procurement pushed for a lower price while security requested evidence on data residency.
customer_reaction: The deal remained in negotiation and the security review became the critical path.
lessons_learned: Price pressure often masks a risk objection; address security evidence early and keep value visible.

customer_context: The bank needed stronger audit trails without extending the implementation timeline.
customer_reaction: Risk approved the plan and the CIO signed off.
lessons_learned: Security objections become manageable when evidence and delivery controls are concrete.

customer_context: The incumbent offered a renewal bundle and the evaluation focused on short-term price.
actions_taken: Waited for the buyer to define success
customer_reaction: The buyer renewed with the incumbent.
lessons_learned: A competitor is difficult to displace when the team does not define a measurable outcome beyond features.

customer_context: The team spent hours reconciling forecasts manually and needed a fast business case.
customer_reaction: Finance approved the project after a six-month payback estimate.
lessons_learned: A small deal can still move quickly when the buyer sees a credible payback and contained onboarding effort.

customer_context: A new revenue leader joined with a mandate to review every sales technology contract.
actions_taken: Re-ran discovery with the new leader
Connected the product to forecast accuracy
customer_reaction: The new leader reopened the evaluation with a clearer success metric.
failed_tactics: Assuming the prior champion's business case carried forward
lessons_learned: After a stakeholder change, re-qualify the business case instead of relying on inherited momentum.

customer_context: The insurer wanted to modernize reporting without replacing the core policy system.
customer_reaction: The team approved a limited first phase and a shared implementation plan.
lessons_learned: Integration proof lowers perceived implementation risk and makes competitive change easier to approve.

customer_context: The buyer saw the operational benefit but feared migration effort and unplanned consulting costs.
customer_reaction: The buyer chose to keep the existing process.
lessons_learned: Price objections paired with implementation risk need a concrete rollout plan before commercial pressure.
